## Truth and contracts

- [ ] Capability claims distinguish implemented behavior from requirements/proposals.
- [ ] Core behavior is linked to exact source, contract, and executable evidence.
- [ ] No normative core schema or business/security rule was forked into the client.
- [ ] Generated artifacts, if any, are reproducible and were not manually patched.
- [ ] Contract/version/lifecycle and backward-compatibility effects are described.

## Architecture and security

- [ ] Flutter/application code does not call HTTP directly; SDK code has no Flutter dependency.
- [ ] No in-app WebView, embedded server page, or hybrid fallback was added.
- [ ] External-browser links, if any, forward no native credential or restricted context and are not claimed as parity.
- [ ] Authentication, authorization, site/context, ETag, idempotency, Problem Details, secrets, caches, downloads, and telemetry impacts are addressed.
- [ ] Permission loss, extension/definition lifecycle, and failure/ambiguous-outcome behavior are covered.

## Experience

- [ ] Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, and iOS impact is recorded, including intentional deferrals.
- [ ] Keyboard, screen reader, focus, text scale, contrast, reduced motion, long/RTL text, exact values, and adaptive layouts are covered where relevant.
- [ ] Loading, empty, validation, denial, conflict, offline/network, progress, and unavailable states are covered.

## Verification

<!-- List exact commands, fixtures, platforms, and results. Do not use screenshots as the only parity evidence. -->

- [ ] Narrow relevant checks passed.
- [ ] Aggregate repository gate passed, or the documented reason it is not yet applicable is stated.
- [ ] Reference/native stored outcome, version, audit, error, and denial evidence is attached for any parity claim.
- [ ] Documentation links, roadmap status, and ADRs are consistent.
